title: Financial Forecasting: Tools and Techniques
overview: Forecasting future events is one of the most challenging aspects of decision-making for professionals. Too often, this challenge is met with an over-reliance on professional judgment and educated guesses. While experience and intuition are valuable, effective forecasting requires structured tools and techniques. This course focuses on equipping participants with practical forecasting methodologies and demonstrates their application through Microsoft Excel.

Participants will gain hands-on experience in using Excel to develop robust financial forecasting models, enabling them to make informed decisions and better support their organizations' strategic goals.
audience: This course is ideal for financial controllers, analysts, finance and accounting managers, supervisors, and finance professionals responsible for creating, interpreting, and maintaining forecasts within their organizations.
methodology: This course is delivered as a hands-on workshop, with participants actively applying forecasting techniques in Microsoft Excel. Through a combination of practical exercises, case studies, and interactive discussions, participants will develop the skills needed to build and interpret effective forecasting models.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Apply a range of forecasting techniques to improve financial and business decision-making.
Utilize Microsoft Excel to create and manage effective forecasting models.
Identify and incorporate macroeconomic and microeconomic factors into forecasts.
Develop detailed models for forecasting income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements.
Distinguish between different forecasting models and approaches and communicate their implications to senior management.

items.text: Correlation coefficient and coefficient of determination
Analyzing their impact on forecasting models
Sales forecasting: market demand, company demand, and sales forecasts
Forecasting cost of sales and operating expenses
Price and cost per unit of activity
Analyzing and interpreting cash flow data
Building alternative scenarios to address uncertainty
Evaluating risks and their impact on forecasting outcomes
